bullets.text: Combined ratio 92.5 beat the 96 target; pretax operating income rose 6% to $1.5B; net income was $1.3B ($2.15/share); ROE 17.2%; comprehensive income trailed 2014 by ~50 cents/share, pressured in part by unrealized losses.
Companywide NPW +10% (+$1.9B) to top $20B, aided by nine months of ASI property premium; NPE finished just short of $20B; Commercial Lines written premium rose mid-teens to exceed $2B.

Total portfolio return was ~1.6% on $21B; Gainshare scored 1.6; declared $0.89/share dividend ($519M); ARX acquisition consumed $877M; repurchased 7.3M shares; completed $400M debt offering; debt-to-capital ended at approximately 27%.

Direct and Agency auto reached rough parity. Direct written premiums grew 11% at a 95.1 CR with near double-digit unit growth. Agency reversed policy count erosion and achieved strong new business inflows.

Introduced Platinum, integrating ASI property and Progressive auto into a single agency bundled product; broadened Destination Era personal offerings to include property, umbrella, flood, classic car, travel, and pet insurance.

Commercial Lines generated an 84 CR with mid-teen growth, potentially earning a #1 commercial auto market share designation. Special Lines grew around 3% with loss costs slightly below expectations and significant motorcycle share.

Advancing Destination Era around 'Robinsons' via Acquire, Anchor, Bundle, Extend strategy; shifting metric of success toward customer life expectancy; estimates addressable market could expand by up to 50% for auto.

Analyzed real-time Snapshot data to understand mileage increases and frequency amid lower gas prices; ingested weather data several times an hour to evaluate loss trends; planning 2016 smartphone Snapshot app introduction.

Enterprise expense ratio was an attractive 20% relative to the industry, contributing to success; management sees opportunities for greater operational leverage, in large part through longer customer relationships.

The 'Sprinkles are for Winners' phrase took on a life of its own. Addressable media beyond network television will attract more acquisition spending, aiding yield analysis and brand advancement for the Destination Era.
